short: Sensors, HMM decoder and class grammar are standard; the 8.9% WER is five of six subjects of the authors' uncited 2014 table (six-subject mean 11.2%).
position: The paper [@meltzner2018development] combines an 11-site face and neck sEMG array with an exhaustive 2,047-subset search (M05), a Kaldi triphone HMM with HLDA, MLLR and SGMM (M06) and a natural-language class grammar (M07); all three are standard against the ledger. Its final-system rows match the group's uncited 2014 report [@deng2014practical]: Table 2's 8.9% WER is the mean of five of the six 2014 subjects, whose six-subject mean is 11.2%, and the omitted subject is not identified and may be one of the three stated exclusions. The 2014 report documents the task-set-disjoint protocol with a validation split that the journal omits; the grammar construction for Corpus 3 is unstated, and "far surpassing previous attempts" compares against other tasks.
